Pre-review (contributor pre-check, read-only; not a collaborator review):

- should-fix - crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_zigzag.rs:67 - The wrap test is `span >= period`, but the seam-edge drop then removes the runs near the loop's own min/max x (pocket_zigzag.rs:106), not the points at the seam copies. On a cover wider than one period, a loop that spans a period while its extremes do not stand on the seam (an island copy larger than a period, or a loop crossing a seam copy at interior x) gets its own extreme ends dropped and its arcs trimmed. That does not follow the seam law and can leave the loop's end walls unringed, silently. Suggest gating the seam path on the loop touching the seam copies (x near 0 or a period multiple within tol), not on span alone.
- note - pocket_zigzag.rs:107-108 - The doc of `seam_open_arcs` says a loop with no seam point comes back whole and open, but flags are taken against the loop's own min/max, so the extreme points are always flagged and the `!any` branch is unreachable. Doc is misleading; code is harmless.
- note - pocket_zigzag.rs:160-171 - `one_period` is sound: the window head saturates (line 156), the crossing divides only when `q.x != p.x` and clamps t to 0..1, and no panic path exists. A loop whose x re-enters the window after leaving is truncated at the first exit - that loses coverage, it never cuts twice.
- note - No-seam path is byte-identical: `rest_passes` delegates with `None`, and `closed_ring` reproduces the old reverse-then-close order exactly; `hsm.rs:147` passes `None` when `seam` is absent, so planar #3129 behaviour is unchanged.
- note - Prime Directive: no unwrap/expect/panic in the new non-test code; degenerate loops (len < 2, all-seam, non-finite bounds) return empty or pass through cleanly.
- note - Law checks pass: clean-room provenance lines present, files under 400 lines, code lives in `crates/motion` (no app-layer rule touched), PR body is ASD-STE100 with a Changelog line and ends `Fixes #3168`; #3168 is open with a live claim.

Pre-review should-fix, pushed as 544d6791e:

The seam gate in the ring code tested whether a boundary loop SPANS the cover period. A period-spanning loop whose extremes stand off the seam was trimmed by the wrong rule. The gate now tests seam CONTACT: a loop that reaches a cover end within the seam's reach wraps the seam (its cover-end edges are the seam's copies at one azimuth); a loop that spans a period mid-cover touches no cover end and closes exactly as the no-seam case does. `zigzag_ringed_passes` now takes the cover ends and seam reach (`SeamWrap`), which `plan_level` maps from its own `Seam`. The wrapped-ring law is intact: a loop that touches a cover end still drops its cover-end edges and keeps one period per arc.

Pinning tests stay meaningful and pass: `the_wrapped_ring_cuts_no_azimuth_twice` and `the_dflat_edge_walls_are_ringed` still fail on the pre-fix code (the pre-fix planner rings no level boundary), and both pass here.

Heavy lanes, `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main` at 544d6791e: all 243 steps pass, 0 failed, wall 49.5 min. Per lane: heavy build (release) ok; motion heavy - lib, bins, doc, and every integration binary (adaptive_hsm, adaptive_troch_*, rotary_adaptive, finish3d, multiaxis, pocket3d_hsm, shape_masks, and the rest) ok; app heavy - lib, bins, doc, and every integration binary (rotary_field_parity, shared_face_bodies_finish, stock_*, lathe_*, mcp, and the rest) ok. The known-fail checks (#1950 x3, #2849) ran and were red as expected. Slow steps over 60 s: motion lib twins, rotary_adaptive, lathe_workholding_kinds, rotary_field_parity, shared_face_bodies_finish - all ok.

Review should-fix in (seam-contact gate, 544d6791e): quick gate green on the final head; heavy lanes 243/243 green (motion + app, run on the previous head and re-verified by the seam tests on this head - state exactly what your quick gate covered).

Needs changes before merge. One blocking finding. Set `needs-rework` because a non-seam wall can lose its finish ring.

### Requested before merge

1. **Blocker — preserve the closing edge of a loop that has no seam vertices.** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_zigzag.rs:125` (called at line 94; gate at line 83).

   The gate selects a loop within `reach` of a cover end. The split then tests vertices against the exact cover bounds. If no vertex matches, this branch returns the points without their closing point. This removes a real wall edge.

   I reproduced this with the unchanged boundary helpers in an isolated Rust probe. Use `SeamWrap { lo: 0.0, hi: 20.0, period: 10.0, reach: 2.0 }`. Use these two periodic rectangles, in the stated order:

   ```text
   [(1.5,2), (8.5,2), (8.5,8), (1.5,8)]
   [(11.5,2), (18.5,2), (18.5,8), (11.5,8)]
   ```

   Both loops enter the seam branch. Neither loop has a seam vertex. Both returned passes omit the last-to-first edge. Thus both copies omit the wall at `x = 1.5 mod 10`. The periodic copy does not restore that wall ring. The rows alone can retain the wall cusps that #3168 must remove.

   Use seam positions consistent with the eroded center boundary. Preserve the cyclic closure when no actual seam run is removed. Add a test with periodic loops near both cover ends. Check both cutting directions.

### Previous findings

No earlier collaborator review exists. The contributor's earlier pre-check concerned the span gate. Commit `544d6791e` replaces that gate. The new gate admits the near-end, non-seam case above. The two supplied pinning tests pass but do not cover this case.

Back to draft: two new commits land on a ready PR. One is the review fix - a near-end ring that owns no seam run now closes, so its wall ring survives (the blocker of the `<!-- pr-reviewer: 544d6791e... -->` review). The other is the refresh merge of origin/main (the pass-start work), with one hand-resolved hunk. The quick gate ran on the final head daf4c9e56 and is green: 167 steps, 0 failed.

Ready again. Refresh class DELTA: the merge of origin/main took one hand-resolved hunk in `crates/motion/src/machining3d/hsm.rs` - main''s `seam.is_none()` guard on the Zigzag ring gate is dropped, because it kept seam levels off the ring path only while the ring code could not wrap a seam; this branch makes it wrap. Main''s pass-start work (#3361, #3362: `start_side`, `side_rings`) is kept whole on the other paths, and the ring test fixture takes the new `pass_start` default. Everything else merged clean.

Quick gate on the final head daf4c9e56, `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 167 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The pinning test `the_near_end_loop_without_a_seam_vertex_keeps_its_closing_edge` covers the review blocker with the reviewer''s own case (`SeamWrap { lo: 0.0, hi: 20.0, period: 10.0, reach: 2.0 }`, the two periodic rectangles, both climb directions); `the_wrapped_ring_cuts_no_azimuth_twice` and `the_dflat_edge_walls_are_ringed` stay green.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings. Replace `needs-rework` with `merge-ready`: the earlier finding is fixed, all local checks pass, and GitHub reports `MERGEABLE`.

### Previous findings

1. **Fixed: a near-end loop must keep its closing wall edge.** Commit `ca198c366` adds the closure guard. The new test `the_near_end_loop_without_a_seam_vertex_keeps_its_closing_edge` passes. It checks both periodic rectangles from the earlier review, in both cutting directions. An isolated probe also passes. Removal of the guard makes that probe fail at the closing-wall assertion.

I checked the author's response and the merge resolution in `hsm.rs`. The resolution enables the seam ring path and keeps main's pass-start handling on the other strategy paths. The planar path still uses the same rows and closed rings.
